verdicts.quote: the timing anchor (for example, due date or issue date), eligibility start, cadence
verdicts.missing: The reminder count and offsets from the invoice due date, including whether any reminder precedes it.

verdicts.quote: The billing policy owner must confirm how partial payments, outstanding credits, drafts, disputed, voided, written-off, reopened and cancelled invoices map to eligibility wherever these states exist.
verdicts.missing: Full settlement suppresses sending. The stopping rules for partial payment, voiding, credits, disputes and payment plans are undecided.

verdicts.quote: source of contact authorization, consent/suppression and multi-recipient rules where applicable
verdicts.missing: How do-not-contact, pause and unsubscribe flags affect reminders, including whether billing notices are exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: Overlapping runs, restart and replay refer to the same logical occurrence within its billing scope. A confirmed handoff for that occurrence prevents a further submission for it.
Before each new handoff attempt, including recovery, establish current eligibility against the billing authority's supported consistency contract.
If recovery cannot safely proceed, including when the retry window or budget is exhausted, stop submissions and expose the blocked or terminal outcome with its reason.
verdicts.missing: When and how often to retry during a provider outage, and when persistent failure triggers an alert to a person.

verdicts.where: Non-functional requirements, Freshness, throughput and cost (R-1–R-4)
verdicts.quote: Scheduling precision, acceptable dispatch delay, burst/workload, invocation and delivery quotas and cost limits are unresolved.
verdicts.missing: The provider's sending limit and how to pace or defer a large batch to stay within it.

verdicts.quote: late-work and catch-up behavior, and how changes apply to existing invoices, past occurrences and in-flight work
verdicts.missing: Which missed steps to send for invoices already overdue at activation and how to prevent an immediate backlog burst.

verdicts.quote: timezone/calendar and precision for computing due instants
verdicts.missing: Whose local time governs sending and which hours, weekend days and holidays allow delivery.

verdicts.quote: A missing, ambiguous, invalid or unauthorized destination or missing required content prevents handoff and leaves an actionable reason.
verdicts.missing: How a bounce reported after handoff affects future attempts to reach that address.

verdicts.quote: The billing policy owner must identify the intended recipient, source of contact authorization, consent/suppression and multi-recipient rules where applicable
verdicts.missing: Which billing contacts receive the reminder when several are authorized.

verdicts.quote: Authorized operations can correlate a scheduled occurrence with suppression, hold, confirmed acceptance, rejection or unresolved outcome and recovery. Delivery evidence, if available, is attributed to the same occurrence.
verdicts.missing: What send details and timestamp each invoice's reminder history shows for each step, and whether that history is visible on the invoice.

verdicts.quote: The received message identifies the invoice and communicates that payment remains outstanding using approved fields.
verdicts.missing: Whether the reminder includes the amount, due date and a way to pay, and whether a payment link expires.

verdicts.quote: The authorized billing policy owner supplies timing policy.
verdicts.missing: Manual sends are outside scope. Who, if anyone, may stop an individual reminder by hand is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Changed or withdrawn policy requires re-evaluation before dispatch.
verdicts.missing: Whether an operator can disable reminders globally or per customer and preview or dry-run them. Manual reminders are outside scope.

verdicts.quote: Authorized operations can correlate a scheduled occurrence with suppression, hold, confirmed acceptance, rejection or unresolved outcome and recovery.
verdicts.missing: Whether and where an operator can see the next planned reminder before it is processed.

verdicts.quote: An occurrence outside the allowed window generates zero submissions and an observable skipped outcome.
verdicts.missing: The maximum permitted lateness or a sending-volume cap. The length of the catch-up window is left to policy.

verdicts.quote: Before and after each evaluation the reminder feature leaves billing records unchanged.
